title: Is Slate Auto’s new electric truck the EV Americans need?
gist: With US EV sales share under 10% and falling, Slate Auto is betting that a stripped-down, sub-$25,000, 205-mile-range electric pickup can succeed where feature-laden, long-range EVs like the discontinued Ford F-150 Lightning failed, backed by nearly $1.4 billion in funding including from Jeff Bezos and validated by China's mass adoption of lower-range, affordable EVs.

themes.theme: US EV market weakness as backdrop

insights.claim: EVs account for under 10% of total new-vehicle sales in the US and that share is declining, even though transportation is the single largest source of US greenhouse-gas emissions.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Sets a bearish macro backdrop against which any new EV entrant, including Slate, must be evaluated — the addressable market is shrinking, not growing.
insights.quote: EVs account for under 10% of total new-vehicle sales in the US, and the numbers are declining.

insights.claim: Roughly half of Americans are struggling to pay for basic necessities like gas and groceries, and 95% believe the country is in an affordability crisis according to a recent Harris poll, creating a demand opening for a genuinely low-cost EV.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Macro affordability pressure is a demand-side catalyst that could favor a stripped-down, sub-$25k EV over feature-laden $50k+ competitors.
insights.quote: 95% of Americans believe we’re in an affordability crisis, according to a recent Harris poll.

insights.claim: Slate Auto is pursuing a deliberately austere strategy — a two-door pickup shorter than a Honda Civic, base-model hand-crank windows, and a small 65 kWh lithium iron phosphate battery giving only 205 miles of range — to price its base model under $25,000, well below the roughly $50,000 US average new-vehicle price.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: A direct bet against industry consensus of chasing range/feature parity with gas cars; if it succeeds, it validates a 'cheap and small' EV segment incumbents have largely ignored.
insights.quote: By accepting a shorter range and forgoing the frills that Americans have come to expect in vehicles, Slate is able to offer the base model of its truck for less than $25,000.

insights.claim: Slate's quoted top range of 205 miles is far below competitors' — the most basic Tesla Model 3 can travel over 320 miles on a charge — underscoring how far Slate has stripped range in favor of price.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Quantifies the range gap investors should weigh when assessing whether Slate's price-for-range trade-off will resonate beyond the most price-sensitive buyers.
insights.quote: For comparison, the most basic Tesla Model 3 can go over 320 miles on a charge.
insights.locator: paragraph on battery and range specs

insights.claim: The author explicitly predicts that Slate's bet — that drivers will accept a small, short-range vehicle in exchange for a low price — will pay off.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: A direct, dated forecast from the author on the affordable-EV thesis, usable as a benchmark against Slate's actual 2026-2027 sales and preorder conversion.
insights.quote: The key question that will determine Slate’s success or failure is whether drivers can get on board with a small, short-range vehicle for the sake of its price tag. At this moment, I’d bet the answer is yes.

insights.claim: The average American driver logs under 35 miles a day, and nearly 90% of personal-vehicle trips are 20 miles or less, undercutting the rationale for large, expensive, long-range EV batteries.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Reframes battery size and range as an oversold feature relative to actual usage — an argument favoring smaller-battery, lower-cost EV designs going forward.
insights.quote: the average driver puts under 35 miles a day on the odometer, and nearly 90% of trips in a personal vehicle are 20 miles or less.
insights.locator: paragraph on daily driving distance data

insights.claim: A recent study found that EV drivers typically use less than 20% of their vehicle's available range on a typical day, reinforcing that current EV battery capacity and cost are oversized relative to real-world need.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Supports a thesis that battery cost — the largest single cost driver in EVs — could be cut significantly without hurting most owners' daily usability, a potential pricing lever for EV makers.
insights.quote: One recent study found that people tend to use less than 20% of their EV’s range on a typical day.
insights.locator: paragraph on EV range usage studies

themes.theme: Ford F-150 Lightning as cautionary comp

insights.claim: Ford discontinued the F-150 Lightning — the flagship hope for US EV adoption, launched in 2021 as an electric version of America's best-selling vehicle — in December 2025, just four years after introduction, due to slashed federal EV tax credits under the second Trump administration combined with escalating vehicle prices.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: A concrete failure case showing a large-battery, range-competitive EV strategy at a major legacy automaker did not survive policy headwinds plus cost inflation — a direct bear comp for any large-battery EV strategy.
insights.quote: Ford discontinued the truck in December 2025, just four years after its introduction.
insights.locator: paragraph on the F-150 Lightning's discontinuation

insights.claim: The F-150 Lightning's base price rose from roughly $40,000 at its 2022 launch to over $54,000 in its final year, driven in part by a battery roughly twice the capacity of Slate's needed to reach near-300-mile range.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Quantifies the direct cost tradeoff between range and price that Slate is explicitly avoiding — a testable causal mechanism for EV unit economics.
insights.quote: The base model cost roughly $40,000 when shipments started in 2022; during its final year, prices topped $54,000.

themes.theme: Global evidence for affordable, lower-range EVs

insights.claim: China already has over 40 million EVs and plug-in hybrids on the road, with roughly half of new vehicles sold being electric, and the average new EV sold there in 2025 had only 247 miles of range, versus 329 miles in the US and 281 in Europe.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: An international comp showing lower-range, more affordable EVs already achieve mass adoption elsewhere, supporting the thesis that Slate's approach is a proven pattern once price is low enough, not a fringe bet.
insights.quote: China currently has over 40 million EVs and plug-in hybrids on the roads, and roughly half of new vehicles sold are electric.
insights.locator: paragraph on China's EV adoption and range data

themes.theme: Slate's funding, scale-up, and incumbent response

insights.claim: Slate has raised nearly $1.4 billion across three major funding rounds, with investors including Jeff Bezos, and plans a factory with 100,000-unit capacity in its first year scaling to 150,000 soon after, with preorder deliveries starting late 2026.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Quantifies the capital and production runway backing the affordable-EV bet — key figures for assessing execution risk and scale economics.
insights.quote: Investors, including Jeff Bezos, have put nearly $1.4 billion into the company over three major funding rounds.
insights.locator: paragraph on Slate's funding and factory capacity

insights.claim: Ford is re-entering the small electric truck segment with its own model expected to debut in 2027 at a retail price of around $30,000, signaling that a legacy incumbent sees validation in the low-cost, small-EV strategy Slate is pioneering.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Incumbent competitive response within roughly a year of Slate's launch suggests the affordable-small-EV segment will get crowded quickly — Slate's first-mover pricing advantage may be short-lived.
insights.quote: The automaker is working on its own small electric truck, which is expected to debut in 2027 at a retail price of around $30,000.
